rv.q: But Bourne's 'Car Man' is so tuned to perfection it will be a great ride whoever's in the driving seats.
Bourne's witty, raunchy and explosive choreography — lots of roughhousing mechanics and their free-spirited girlfriends — has the flavour of West Side Story and the dramatic tension of pure theatre.
It’s bold, passionate, thrilling and utterly captivating.
It is a powerful experience in the theatre with beautiful music, fascinating choreography and outstanding performances from every member of the cast.
Making a feature of sweat and heavy breathing, it’s well-oiled pulp fiction in dance form and damn gripping stuff.
This isn't just a dance production, it's an epic theatrical event
This remains after all this time a genuine thriller albeit one built on bodies rather than plot twists.
But strictly as a dance piece, this is spectacular to look at, impeccably staged and performed with limitless brio.
Directed by a master of his craft who seems poised to continue moving from strength to strength, this immaculate remounting is truly not to be missed.
What a masterpiece this production is.
Matthew Bourne's The Car Man is about as good as it gets.

Luca (played by Harrison Dowzell) is the new guy in town and quickly finds work at Dino’s garage. But heartthrob Luca is less interested in tinkering with car motors than Dino’s (Danny Reubens) younger, attractive wife Lana (Cordelia Braithwaite).
The Car Man is a slick, stylish and thoroughly entertaining piece of dance theatre.
It’s a scorcher of a show made for these hot summer nights.
All elements are to one of the highest standards within the world with regards to how to put on a dance show, and will continue to draw crowds for years to come.
The way Brotherston’s two-storey construction of scaffolding morphs from garage and office below and showers and living quarters above, to a seedy nightclub and then dark prison is utter genius.
It might not be my favourite Bourne work, but it is still a bloody good show and, at £110 in the stalls, a reliable seat buy.
The Car Man will never be topped.
Adventures production is a masterclass in dance theatre—thrilling, seductive, emotionally charged and utterly unforgettable.
Bourne and his New Adventures company of dancers, together with masterly set designer Lez Brotherston and lighting director Chris Davey, create a powerful atmosphere from the beginning.
Mattheq Bourne's The Car Man is slick, super stylish, and so, so sexy.

cn.t: Critics unanimously praise Matthew Bourne's "The Car Man" as a thrilling, sexy dance-noir masterpiece, celebrating its passionate choreography, gripping storytelling, and electrifying fusion of Bizet's Carmen with 1950s Americana pulp fiction.
